ONCOLOGY TRIAL PROTOCOL SUMMARY — Study ONC-2291

## Overview

ONC-2291 is a randomised, open-label Phase III study evaluating pembrolizumab
plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone in patients with previously
untreated advanced non-small-cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC).

## Eligibility Criteria

Patients must be over 18 years of age. Histologically confirmed stage IIIB or
stage IV NSCLC is required. Patients must have an ECOG performance status of 0
or 1. Adequate organ function is required, defined as absolute neutrophil count
of at least 1500 per microlitre and platelet count of at least 100,000 per
microlitre.

Patients with known EGFR sensitising mutations or ALK rearrangements are
excluded. Prior systemic therapy for advanced disease is not permitted. Patients
with untreated central nervous system metastases are excluded.

## Biomarkers

PD-L1 expression is assessed centrally by immunohistochemistry and reported as
tumour proportion score (TPS). Patients are stratified by PD-L1 TPS of at least
50 percent versus less than 50 percent. Tumour mutational burden (TMB) is
measured on archival tissue where available. EGFR and ALK status are determined
at screening for eligibility purposes.

## Endpoints

The primary endpoint is overall survival (OS), defined as time from
randomisation to death from any cause. The key secondary endpoint is
progression-free survival (PFS), assessed by blinded independent central review
per RECIST version 1.1. Additional secondary endpoints include objective
response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DoR). Patient-reported outcomes
are assessed as an exploratory endpoint.

## Treatment Regimen

Pembrolizumab 200 mg is administered intravenously every three weeks for up to
35 cycles. Carboplatin is dosed to an area under the curve of 5 on day 1 of each
21-day cycle. Pemetrexed 500 mg per square metre is given on day 1 of each
cycle. Treatment continues until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or
completion of 35 cycles.

## Adverse Events

Adverse events are graded per CTCAE version 5.0. Immune-mediated adverse events
of special interest include pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, and
hypophysitis. Grade 3 or higher pneumonitis requires permanent discontinuation
of pembrolizumab. Dose reduction of chemotherapy is permitted; dose reduction of
pembrolizumab is not permitted.

## Safety Monitoring

An independent data monitoring committee reviews unblinded safety data every six
months. Enrolment must be halted if the rate of grade 5 treatment-related events
exceeds 2 percent in either arm.
